item.title: China Tankers Head to Red Sea Chokepoint Despite Houthi Attacks
item.description: Two China-owned oil tankers loaded with Saudi Arabian crude are sticking to their course toward the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el Mandeb, despite Houthi militants attacking vessels in the region overnight.

item.title: EasyJet Profit Falls 70% Amid Higher Fuel Bill, Lower Demand
item.description: EasyJet Plc said profit fell by 70% in its fiscal third quarter as the UK budget carrier continues to suffer from higher jet fuel costs and lower consumer demand, driven by the impact from the Middle East conflict.

item.title: BT Profit Falls as Broadband, Voice Margins Offset Cuts
item.description: BT Group Plc reported a slight decline in profits for its fiscal first quarter, as lower margins in its broadband and voice businesses offset its cost-cutting efforts.

item.title: Absa Nears Tanzania Deal to Combine $3 Billion of Banking Assets
item.description: Absa Group Ltd. is nearing a deal to combine its banking interests in Tanzania as the lender looks to increase the scale of its East African businesses, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: China Cuts AI Gap as Moonshot Shows Zhipu Isn’t One-Off, BI Says
item.description: Chinese AI models narrowed the performance gap with US counterparts to a record-low 6% in June, down from 9% in May, which Bloomberg Intelligence said raises questions about the sustainability of US technological supremacy in the sector.

item.title: TotalEnergies Profit Jumps 68% as War Upends Energy Markets
item.description: TotalEnergies SE said second-quarter profit surged as the Iran war boosted prices of crude and refined products, offsetting a drop in profits in its gas business.

item.title: Airtel Mobile-Money Unit Chooses London for Listing Location
item.description: Airtel Africa Plc picked London as the primary listing location for its mobile-money business and expects to start trading there this year.

item.title: FTSE 100: Stocks and Bonds Fall as Oil Marches Higher
item.description: FTSE 100: Stocks and Bonds Fall as Oil Marches Higher【原文：FTSE 100: Stocks and Bonds Fall as Oil Marches Higher】

item.title: AI Data Center Boom Sparks 80% Surge in First-Half FDI Applications to Thailand
item.description: Foreign investors applied to invest 1.37 trillion baht ($40.6 billion) in Thailand in the first half of 2026, up 80% from a year earlier, amid a wave of investments in artificial intelligence and data center projects.

item.title: Hong Kong, Malaysia Collaborate to Broaden Cross-Market Access
item.description: Hong Kong and Malaysia will work together to expand access to capital and deepen cross-border participation in both markets as they look to attract more international investment.

item.title: China Curbs Loan Structure Widely Used by Distressed Developers
item.description: China is restricting real estate companies from using a popular offshore loan structure that has helped some of them weather the country’s property crisis, according to people familiar with the matter, adding to recent moves to strengthen oversight of overseas borrowing.

item.title: Roche Quarterly Sales Held Back by Blockbuster Eye Drug
item.description: Roche Holding’s results showed a slower-than-expected recovery for eye blockbuster Vabysmo as investors look to a key new drug to power growth ahead.

item.title: Burnham Cuts Business Rates on Pubs, Clubs and Live Venues
item.description: The UK will cut tax on pubs, social clubs and some live music venues across England, as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham marks his first week in power with a string of promises to lower the cost of living.

item.title: China Bond Rally Shows Weak Economic Sentiment Before Politburo
item.description: China’s sovereign bonds are rallying once again as economic weakness, sliding stocks and expectations for greater monetary policy support revive demand for fixed-income assets.

item.title: PHP/USD: Philippines Draws Line in Sand for Peso Weakness as Oil Surges
item.description: A potential line in the sand is forming for the Philippine peso at its record low, even as the central bank maintains it doesn’t defend a specific level.

item.title: STMicro Plunges as Weak Forecast Eclipses Fourth-Quarter Outlook
item.description: STMicroelectronics NV plunged the most in a year after the chipmaker forecast third-quarter sales that missed analysts’ expectations, dimming hopes for a stronger recovery on the back of artificial intelligence data center demand.

item.title: Nokia’s Profit Beats Estimates as Data Centers Boost Growth
item.description: Nokia’s second-quarter profit strongly beat analysts’ forecasts, as the Finnish mobile network equipment maker’s push to supply gear to data centers propelled sales.

item.title: India’s Top Asset Manager Said to Plan $200 Million Tech Fund
item.description: SBI Funds Management is planning its first technology-focused fund for private firms, people familiar with the matter said, as India’s largest asset manager follows rivals in bulking up in the fast-growing alternative investment fund industry.

item.title: BNP’s Stock Traders Ride Wall Street Rally With 43% Gain
item.description: BNP Paribas SA reported better-than-expected results for the second quarter as its stock traders blew past analysts’ estimates, in a sign that the rally that fueled record results on Wall Street spilled over into Europe.

item.title: Zimbabwe’s State Firm Secures $300 Million to Develop Lithium Mine
item.description: Mutapa Energy Resources, Zimbabwe’s state-owned lithium miner, has secured $300 million from a group of companies, which includes Chinese entities, to develop its facilities in the southern African nation.

item.title: Dassault Systèmes to Buy Drug Trial Software Firm for $2 Billion
item.description: Dassault Systèmes SE will buy drug trial software maker ArisGlobal for as much as $2 billion as the French firm expands its push into life sciences.

item.title: Singapore Core Inflation Quickens to 1.6% Ahead of MAS Decision
item.description: Singapore’s core inflation accelerated last month as higher global energy costs are beginning to filter through to consumer prices.

item.title: Crop Prices Hit 3-Year High as Black Sea Attacks, Heat Stoke Food Inflation
item.description: Crop prices rose to a three-year high as heat waves and escalating attacks in the Black Sea threaten to disrupt global grain trade, reviving risks to food inflation that have also been stoked by the war in Iran.

item.title: India RBI Says Economy Resilient Despite Monsoon, Iran War Risks
item.description: India’s central bank reiterated that the economy remains resilient, but the Iran war and a deficient monsoon could pose risks to the outlook, according to its monthly economic report.

item.title: ECB Rate Decision: Lagarde Set to Keep Policy Unchanged to Gauge Iran War Risks
item.description: The European Central Bank will probably keep interest rates on hold on Thursday, buying time to assess the fallout of renewed fighting in the Middle East.

item.title: Half of Economists Still See BOJ Waiting Until December to Hike
item.description: Half of surveyed economists still expect the Bank of Japan to wait until December to bump its benchmark interest rate higher, with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government seen as a key obstacle to further action, according to a Bloomberg survey.

item.title: China’s Semight Is Said to Mull Hong Kong Listing After 2,200% Stock Rise
item.description: Semight Instruments Co. is considering a second listing in Hong Kong, people familiar with the matter said, after shares of the Chinese maker of test instruments for semiconductors surged roughly 2,200% since their debut in April.

item.title: Indonesian Stocks Rise 20% From Low in June, Set for Bull Market
item.description: A rally in Indonesian stocks put the nation’s benchmark index on track for a bull market, helped by a regional rebound as well as a recent credit-rating announcement.

item.title: India Rate-Hike Odds Rise as Pricey Crude Stokes Inflation Risk
item.description: The swap market is pricing in at least a 25-basis-point hike at the October meeting.

item.title: China Solar Lobby Says Fewer Installs Mark Sustainable Shift
item.description: China’s solar lobby said the industry is on a more sustainable track, after a policy shift drove a 66% decline in installations in the first half of 2026.
